input.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
input.rationale: Section 11 selects Arizona law, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), and Section 19 sends all Disputes to mandatory binding arbitration under U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules rather than to a court forum, with no agreed venue. The redline moves governing law to New York and substitutes exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, matching the preferred position, while leaving the surrounding severability and dispute-scope language intact. Delaware or California law and courts remain available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Switch governing law from Arizona to New York and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the courts in New York County
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have changed the governing law from Arizona to New York and replaced the mandatory arbitration forum with the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, since our playbook accepts only New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales law with a court forum rather than arbitration. If New York is difficult for you, we can accept Delaware or California law and courts as a fallback.

ops.oldText: the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
ops.newText: the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

ops.oldText: will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com). Any award or order rendered by the arbitrator may be confirmed as a judgment or order in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction, which includes within the federal judicial district of the residence of the party against whom such award or order was entered.
ops.newText: will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York, and each party irrevocably consents to the personal jurisdiction of such courts and waives any objection to venue therein.
